DONE. 602 lines left core for a new slurm4s-batch module.

Moved to io.github.bbuchsbaum.slurm4s.batch: axes, grids and their cross products, the Argument opaque type, the ArgValue typeclass and its Mirror-based ScriptArguments derivation, language command prefixes, sharding, gang plans, batch topology, and BatchPlanner. Core keeps identifiers, resources, launch specification, job identity, reported state and evidence, the submit/query/cancel result models, and Scheduler[F] — the scheduler kernel and nothing else.

The extraction was clean, which is itself evidence the boundary was real: nothing else in core referenced any batch type, and Batch.scala used no core-private members beyond its own (private[core] became private[batch]). The build graph gained one edge — batch sits between core and protocol, because protocol's wire codecs genuinely carry batch topology and arguments.

Grid.product fixed while moving, since the move is what made it visible:
- size is Long. It was Int, and a product of two large grids overflows Int long before it exhausts the heap.
- product returns Either[BatchPlanFailure, Grid[(A, B)]] and refuses beyond Grid.MaximumRows (1,000,000). Two 100k-row grids previously produced a 10^10-element flatMap that OOMed with no typed failure — while the resource arithmetic three hundred lines below had careful Int.MaxValue guarding. The row count had none.
- Grid.cross carries that refusal outward rather than hiding it, so the failure surfaces where a grid is actually built. Two tests: a 2000x2000 product is refused with TooManyElements; an ordinary 3x3 still builds.

One lowering representation is preserved. No separate batch IR was introduced — batch compiles to the same BatchPlan the protocol and worker already consume, and the scheduler still sees only LaunchSpec.

Housekeeping, same limitation as before: this session cannot delete files. modules/core/.../core/Batch.scala and modules/core/src/test/.../core/BatchSuite.scala are emptied to zero bytes and must be removed; their contents live in modules/batch.

Verification: full suite 425 green (2 new), zero warnings under -Werror, scalafmt clean.
